Where's the biggest bottleneck, and what should I fix first?", "public_research": "## Public-information research memo — The Peach Bucket (India)

**Scope:** Public storefront, product-page text, a relevant India-parent Reddit discussion, and general safety guidance. No sales, traffic, checkout, inventory, ad, customer, cost, or account data were available—so the actual commercial bottleneck **cannot be diagnosed conclusively**.

### Strongest public signal: the flagship product is not purchasable
The clearest, highest-priority issue visible publicly is **availability / purchase-path integrity**. The homepage lists the 6-in-1 kit at **₹3,299**, but also displays **“Out of stock”** and a **“Sold out”** purchase button. In the same above-fold area it says **“Only 48 kits left”** with delivery in 2–7 days. Those messages conflict, and a visitor who wants the flagship bundle appears unable to buy it. ([thepeachbucket.com](https://thepeachbucket.com/))

**Implication:** Before changing messaging, price, ads, or the bundle, verify that the main SKU is truly purchasable across landing page, product page, cart, checkout, inventory, and fulfillment rules—and ensure stock/urgency/delivery copy is generated from the same source of truth. This is the first public-facing issue to resolve because a sold-out CTA can suppress conversion regardless of traffic quality or page persuasiveness.

### Secondary public friction: trust claims outrun visible proof
The site presents a premium, reassurance-led proposition: “Top 1% of Indian Parents,” “Made in India,” food-grade/BPA-free materials, 30-day money-back guarantee, 720-day replacement guarantee, and free 1-to-1 video installation support. These are **brand claims**, not independently verified facts in the reviewed public materials. ([thepeachbucket.com](https://thepeachbucket.com/products/the-peach-bucket-6-in-1-child-safety-kit))

However, the crawled product page contained **no detectable review text**. The page also makes comparative assertions about alternatives—e.g., “mass produced with zero quality checks” and “no money back guarantee”—without naming a comparison set or substantiation. ([thepeachbucket.com](https://thepeachbucket.com/products/the-peach-bucket-6-in-1-child-safety-kit))

For a ₹3,299 bundle in a category where adhesive strength, fit, durability, child resistance, and installation matter, the page currently gives detailed *claims* but limited visible *evidence*. That may be a conversion concern, but public data cannot show whether it is the primary loss point.

**Evidence worth validating before adding more persuasion:** authentic customer reviews/photos, examples of Indian switchboard and furniture compatibility, installation video, warranty eligibility/exclusions, material/test documentation where applicable, and precise evidence for the “Made in India,” food-grade, BPA-free, and quality-control claims.

### Audience / product-fit observations
The bundle covers corners/edges, sockets, cabinets, doors, and fridge/microwave access, positioning itself around common Indian-home fixtures and offering 10 five-amp plus two 15-amp socket guards. ([thepeachbucket.com](https://thepeachbucket.com/)) This is a coherent “one organised kit” offer for parents entering the crawling/toddler stage.

A recent **India-specific Reddit thread** is only anecdotal (very low engagement; not representative), but it aligns with the category logic: commenters identified outlet covers and cabinet locks as useful, while reporting that some corner guards could be peeled off and some locks became ineffective. It also shows consumers comparing individual, lower-cost products through FirstCry. ([reddit.com](https://www.reddit.com/r/MomAndBabyIndia/comments/1u3sdpu/baby_proofing_items_that_actually_works/?utm_source=openai))

**Interpretation:** The bundle’s customer-facing differentiation should be demonstrable reliability and home-specific fit—not merely comprehensiveness. The Reddit evidence is insufficient to establish demand prevalence, price sensitivity, or product quality expectations across India.

### Safety and compliance caution
General child-safety guidance supports cabinets/drawers locks for restricting access to medicines, cleaners, matches, knives, and similar hazards, but stresses correct installation, maintenance, and that no device is completely childproof. It also highlights hazards outside this six-part bundle, notably furniture/TV tip-overs. ([cpsc.gov](https://www.cpsc.gov/safety-education/safety-guides/kids-and-babies/Childproofing-Your-Home?utm_source=openai))

That source is **U.S. guidance, not India-specific regulation**. India’s BIS provides a searchable standards system, but this review did **not** identify a verified applicable Indian Standard, certification, or test report for this kit. ([bis.gov.in](https://www.bis.gov.in/know-your-standard/?lang=en&utm_source=openai)) Therefore, safety claims should not be treated as compliance evidence.

### Priority conclusion
**First fix:** Resolve the public contradiction between **“out of stock/sold out”** and **“only 48 kits left / delivery in 2–7 days,”** then validate the end-to-end ability to purchase the flagship kit. This is the only clearly observable, potentially total purchase-path blocker.

**Do not infer:** that stock status is definitely the reason sales are below target; it could be a theme/app rendering issue, intentional waitlisting, a temporary inventory condition, or a crawl artifact. That uncertainty cannot be resolved without storefront/admin and analytics access.

### Exact access gaps
Unavailable public evidence prevents determining whether the largest *business* bottleneck is:
- traffic volume or traffic intent;
- landing-page conversion, add-to-cart rate, checkout completion, payment/COD friction, or delivery coverage;
- stockouts, cancellations, fulfillment performance, or returns;
- price competitiveness, contribution margin, or acquisition economics;
- customer satisfaction, repeat purchase, or warranty claim rates;
- whether the live shopper experience differs by device, PIN code, payment method, or campaign URL."}
